description: This bar chart, from the paper "Morphosyntactic probing of multilingual BERT models," illustrates the mean effect values for six different multilingual BERT models—mBERT-L₂, mBERT-R₂, mBERT-B₂, XLM-L₂, XLM-R₂, and XLM-B₂—across eight linguistic categories: IE-Baltic, IE-Germanic, IE-Indic, IE-Romance, IE-Slavic family, IE-other, Isolate, and Uralic. The horizontal axis lists these linguistic categories in order from left to right, while the vertical axis, labeled "effect," is scaled linearly from 0 to 30, with tick marks at intervals of 10. Each linguistic category is represented by a group of six colored bars, corresponding to the six models as defined in the legend: mBERT-L₂ (light blue), XLM-L₂ (dark blue), mBERT-R₂ (light green), XLM-R₂ (dark green), mBERT-B₂ (light pink), and XLM-B₂ (dark red). Error bars, extending above and below each bar, indicate the standard deviation or uncertainty of the mean effect for each model-category combination. The bars are not sorted; they appear in the order of the linguistic categories on the x-axis. The chart visually emphasizes the Uralic category with a gray bar, which is significantly shorter than all other bars, indicating a very low effect for all models in this group. The tallest bars are found in the IE-Indic category, with mBERT-R₂ and mBERT-B₂ reaching approximately 20 and 22, respectively, and XLM-B₂ reaching approximately 21. The shortest bars are in the Uralic category, with all models showing effects near zero, and in the Isolate category, where all bars are also very short, with values around 1 or less.
